reasoning_traces.think:
The primitives formalize how performance feedback transforms into behavioral responses. The core mechanism is a recursive belief update: players compare their current output to chosen benchmarks (self, team, league), generating residual signals. These signals drive motivation via goal-setting theory (Locke & Latham, 1990) and social comparison theory (Festinger, 1985). However, the system exhibits dual dynamics: positive residuals reinforce effort, while negative residuals trigger either problem-solving or defensive avoidance. The multi-referent framework introduces cross-layer interference—when different benchmarks disagree, the resulting motivational pressure becomes mathematically ill-defined, leading to empirical volatility in player responses. Crucially, public social feedback (e.g., Shaq's critique) acts as an exogenous shock to the belief system, accelerating the update frequency and biasing posterior distributions toward extreme outcomes.
